=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:244, 415-426, 533-543 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Attached shell `-c` arguments such as `sh -c'mysql -pS3cretPass'` bypass nested-command parsing, leaving credentials unmasked in the reported command and command shape.
  WHY: The lexer combines the attached flag and command into one token that the anchored `_SHELL_COMMAND_FLAG_RE` does not match, so `_command_line_credentials()` is not called and the secret is posted.

- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:243, 534-543 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Shells omitted from `_SHELL_COMMAND_RUNNERS`, including `fish`, bypass nested-command parsing and can expose credentials in permission-prompt reports.
  WHY: For an omitted shell such as `fish -c 'mysql -pS3cretPass'`, the runner check fails, so the inner command is not parsed and the password remains unmasked.

- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:184-185, 249 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The URL userinfo patterns can match `@` in a query or fragment when the URL has no path, corrupting valid URLs such as `https://example.com?email=test@example.com`.
  WHY: The patterns do not stop at `?` or `#`, so query or fragment text is mistaken for userinfo; severity disagreement: the highest reported severity is MAJOR, while openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_2 rated it NIT.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
